neighbours.label: The second member of a complementary pair joined by 'and/or' (northern and southern, upper and lower, rural and urban): the word that completes a two-sided whole, vs the same word used alone
fire: During the war the kingdom lost its eastern and western provinces to rival princes.
The ship's upper and lower decks were flooded within an hour of the collision.
Settlers moved into the northern and southern valleys after the treaty was signed.
The bridge links the eastern and western halves of the old city across the river.
Engineers replaced the inner and outer walls of the reactor during the shutdown.
Rebels took control of the western and eastern borderlands by the end of the year.
The museum's left and right wings were added a century after the main hall.
Traders crossed between the northern and southern ports twice every season.
quiet: During the war the kingdom lost its richest provinces to rival princes.
The ship's cargo deck was flooded within an hour of the collision.
Settlers moved into the fertile valleys after the treaty was signed.
The bridge links the two halves of the old city across the river.
Engineers replaced the concrete walls of the reactor during the shutdown.
Rebels took control of the remote borderlands by the end of the year.
The museum's newest wing was added a century after the main hall.
Traders crossed between the busy ports twice every season.

predictions: The second word of a directional or antonym pair (X and Y) reaches 0.3-0.8; the same word without the paired first member stays under 0.1.
short: second half of a complementary pair
